crime_highlights: The appellant sexually assaulted his half sister in the stairwell of a motel.
His half sister told him to stop, but he did not.
His half sister was scared, but tried to act normally.
She became pregnant, but did not tell anybody at the time about the incident or the pregnancy.
rationale_highlights: The reports outlined the appellant's exceptionally difficult and disadvantaged background.
the circumstances of the offender, especially the tremendous challenges he faces, render an actual custodial sentence in this case unfit

Given the dramatically disadvantaged aboriginal background endured by the appellant, a two year order maximises the possibility that the objectives of the youth sentencing regime will be achieved in fact.
note: Youth sentence; Crown conceded custody unfit given offender's circumstances.

crime_highlights: Mr. Ned followed a woman who was confined to a wheelchair from the Skytrain Metrotown station and took an iPad device from her wheelchair.
The woman relied on the device, together with sign language, in order to communicate, as she was unable to hear or speak.
The woman sustained injuries to her neck and arms from the assault and a minor cut when struck by Mr. Ned while he was making his escape.
rationale_highlights: Both men are of aboriginal heritage, and both faced serious difficulties as youths
The sentencing judge took into account Mr. Ned's difficult upbringing and his aboriginal background
Having considered the goal of rehabilitation, the sentencing judge concluded that that goal had to yield to the need to address denunciation and deterrence
note: Court only notes background was considered; no stated effect on sentence.

crime_highlights: he essentially used excessive force in a fight
Mr. Patrick once having started into the fight could not stop and did not stop himself until others intervened.
He did considerable physical damage to Mr. Balczer.
rationale_highlights: She was well aware of the Gladue principles that had to be applied at both sentence proceedings.
It was the entire background of the appellant that impelled her to seek rehabilitation without custody, to no avail as it turned out.
note: Appeal court says Gladue was addressed; no clear statement of reduced culpability.
